title: China harvests FIRST desert-grown oats in Xinjiang's Taklamakan Desert, the largest in country
summary: China has successfully harvested the first batch of desert-grown oats in the Taklamakan Desert, the largest in the country. Approximately 133 hectares of oat fields were planted in April in large round patterns. To improve soil quality and fertilize the fields, relay cropping was used, planting alfalfa between the oat crops. Alfalfa, a drought-resistant forage grass, can be harvested multiple times a year. This method of relay cropping enhances land utilization, increases yields, and benefits the environment.
